messages:
maria: quick heads-up — onboarding fenris-liteq (int8) on canary and noticed structured output flips when dynamic batch packing is on. repro below, short thread.

dan: ugh, flip as in field order change or content mismatch? sample?

maria: field order and occasionally args array shuffled between two near-identical invocations. pasted two raw responses from same prompt run back-to-back: 

maria: run A (no packing, batch_size=1):
{"tool": "search", "args": ["weather", "Seattle"], "meta": {"request_id": "r1", "order": [0]}}

maria: run B (packing enabled, batch_size=4):
{"tool": "search", "args": ["Seattle", "weather"], "meta": {"request_id": "r2", "order": [0]}}

jun: that looks like a batch-packing alignment bug where token offsets shift and the generator emits args in the token interleaving order. seen this before with kv-prefixes + caching.

eva: any numbers? how bad is it on canary vs float baseline?

maria: small A/B over 2k samples: float32, packing off => parse-fail 0.3%, structured-field-order anomalies ~0.05%. int8 (fenris-liteq) + packing on => parse-fail 2.6%, anomalies ~1.8%. so regression is material for tool-calling flows.

dan: yikes. can you capture the batch metadata (batch_id, packing_map) + model kv cache offset for failing traces? we need to correlate with packing boundaries.

maria: yes i grabbed traces for three failures and one golden. included keys: batch_id, shard_idx, pack_map, kv_offset. looks correlated: failures cluster when pack_map crosses token-boundary near prompt suffix.

jun: quick mitigation: runtime flag to enforce preserve-order (serialize outputs per-request after generation) or disable packing for canary until we root cause. preserve-order adds latency but keeps correctness.

eva: cost/latency tradeoff? how much overhead?

maria: microbench: preserve-order + int8 => +8-12ms p50 on our canary config, p99 unchanged for this load. parse-failure drops to baseline ~0.4%.

dan: deploy plan: roll preserve-order as a soft flag on the fenris-liteq canary pool for 24h, collect parse-fail telemetry, then decide. also add packing_map + kv_offset to structured telemetry for future bisection.

ops-bot: deploying runtime flag 'preserve_order_for_toolcalls' to canary pool fenris-liteq-1 now. will route 5% traffic.

maria: thanks — i'll attach the failing trace ids to the canary ticket and run a targeted bisect (pack size sweep + kv offset sampling). next steps: (1) collect more traces, (2) enable preserve-order on canary, (3) run small quantized A/B to verify quality/latency, (4) create quick unit test that simulates interleaved token streams to catch regressions.

dan: assignable? i can take the telemetry + test harness. jun can dig into kernel ordering / packer. eva can run extended A/B.

maria: perfect. i'll open the ticket with links to traces and the A/B numbers. tagging @dan @jun @eva.

ops-bot: ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/INF-3242 (fenris-liteq dynamic-batch schema-drift).

maria: closing loop here — incremental triage scheduled for tomorrow 10:00am PT.
